messages:
samir: Heads-up — we're rolling out a breaking change to how code snippets and interactive examples are embedded in the docs. Old `<!-- example: ... -->` markers are being replaced with the new JSON-LD style block (`<!-- redwood:example { ... } -->`) so the previewer can extract metadata (language, runtime, mock inputs) reliably.

maria: Ok — is this just parsing? any action needed for existing docs repos?

samir: Short answer: yes, a small migration. We have a conversion script that handles 95% of cases but manual review is required for multi-file examples and embedded shell sessions. Migration timeline in short:
- week 0 (now): announcement & migration tool (alpha)
- week 1: automated migration run for smaller repos + docs CI checks enabled
- week 2: enforced lint rule in docs CI (will fail builds)
- week 3: hard redirect and deprecation notice removed from UI

samir: The tool is at repos/docs-tools/migrate-snippets and can be run locally: 

```
# dry-run (won't write files)
python3 -m redwood_snippets.migrate --path docs/ --dry-run

# apply changes
python3 -m redwood_snippets.migrate --path docs/ --apply --backup
```

samir: It emits a report and writes backups to `.redwood-snippet-backups/` by default. Please run locally and open a PR — we'll run org-level migrations for monorepos later.

tj: What about SDK examples that depend on snippet variables? e.g. our JS quickstart references `{{API_KEY}}` in the text — will those still work?

samir: Yes — the JSON-LD block includes a `vars` map. Example: 

```
<!-- redwood:example {"language":"js","entry":"quickstart.js","vars":{"API_KEY":"${{REDACT}}"}} -->
```

samir: The previewer preserves templating and will mask secrets. For programmatic samples (tests/quickstart) the migration also converts legacy fences like ```run:node to `runner: node` metadata in the block.

maria: Is there an eslint/remark plugin to catch old markers?

samir: Yes — we shipped `remark-redwood-snippets` v0.2. It includes a fixer for the common pattern and a lint rule `redwood/snippet-format`. We'll add it to the docs repo CI starter in the next patch.

hana: I'll schedule a 30m sync for tutorials owners to walk through the script. Probably tomorrow 10am PT.

maria: Timeline question — when should teams stop relying on the old previewer behavior?

samir: If you need extra time, file a docs-compat ticket and we'll opt you out for up to 2 weeks. After week 2 the CI rule will block merges. After week 3 the old previewer will be removed from the site (redirects in place).

tj: Anything SDK-side? do language samples need to be updated before migration?

samir: Minimal changes: mainly metadata in the snippet header. If you maintain inline samples in SDK READMEs, run the tool and verify. We'll also cut minor SDK sample releases with updated README examples for JS/Py/Go — expect them in the next 48h.

docs-bot: Reminder: migration tool v0.1 released — https://git.redwood.example/docs-tools/pkgs/migrate-snippets · running the tool in dry-run mode is recommended before apply.

maria: Cool, thanks. I'll start a migration PR for the integrations repo and tag relevant owners.

hana: I can help triage failures from the auto-run. Please @hana in your PRs if you want assistance.

samir: Thanks all. Quick checklist for owners: run the migration script, fix any multi-file examples, add `remark-redwood-snippets` to your CI, open PRs with backups attached. Ping me if you hit edge cases (multi-language cells, live terminal sessions). :shipit:
